mood.summary: Investors are nervous. The Fear & Greed index has sat in Extreme Fear for two weeks, and bearish individual investors outnumber bulls by about 9 points, well below the long-run norm. The S&P 500 fell for a second week and is about 2.5% off its Oct 6 record, while the Nasdaq is about 6% off after its worst day since June on Oct 22. Worries centre on AI spending, oil above $110 on Middle East tensions, and a possible Fed hike in December. Very fearful readings have often come before rebounds, but they don't say when.

trending.note: Board as of Wednesday 4:15 PM ET; prices are the Nov 4 close. Why-it's-trending notes summarize the Stocktwits stream and the news it links to.

items.name: BlackBerry
items.about: Sells cybersecurity software and the QNX operating system used in cars and embedded devices.
items.why: The stock rose about 6.9% on the day to a session high at the close, then eased to $8.71 after hours. The posts that explain it cite no company news; they talk about a run toward $9 and a promoter-style options post, so treat the cause as unconfirmed.

items.name: Micron Technology
items.about: Makes DRAM and NAND memory chips used in data centers, PCs and phones.
items.why: Micron fell about 7% as chip stocks were sold broadly (the 3x semiconductor ETF SOXL lost about 9% and Nvidia 3%). Posts tie the move to worries about a pause in AI data-center spending and to election-day positioning, but no Micron-specific news turned up.

items.name: NVIDIA
items.about: Designs the GPUs and systems that power most AI training and inference.
items.why: Nvidia slid about 3.2% to roughly $200 in the same chip selloff that hit Micron and SOXL. Posts link it to AI data-center spending concerns, including a newsletter on data-center pauses; no company-specific announcement was found.

items.name: Galaxy Digital
items.about: Crypto-focused financial firm that also develops AI data-center capacity in Texas.
items.why: Galaxy dropped about 17% after a Yahoo Finance piece shared in posts said management delayed a major data-center lease to protect shareholder value. Posts say the sell-off also hit other AI-infrastructure and bitcoin-miner names like IREN and CoreWeave.

items.name: AppLovin
items.about: Runs an AI-driven mobile advertising platform for app developers.
items.why: AppLovin rose 11% in the session and about 20% more after hours on its quarterly report. Posts citing the release show adjusted EPS of $4.30 versus $4.07 expected and revenue of $2.19B versus $2.08B expected.

items.name: Vistra
items.about: Texas-based power producer selling electricity from gas, nuclear and solar plants, a supplier to data centers.
items.why: Vistra fell about 14% to near $120. Posts group it with other AI power and data-center names selling off even after the election, and some mention the upcoming earnings report; no company announcement was found.

items.name: Snap
items.about: Parent of Snapchat, a camera and messaging app, and Spectacles AR glasses.
items.why: Snap rose about 5.8% ahead of its quarterly report, which posts say is due this week. A promotional options-flow post says about 84% of options money is in calls, but that is unconfirmed positioning, not news.

items.name: Qualcomm
items.about: Designs Snapdragon phone chips and licenses wireless patents.
items.why: Qualcomm rose 4.7% in the session, then fell to about $166 after hours on its report. Posts quoting the release cite adjusted EPS around $2.17 to $2.21 versus $2.16 expected, December-quarter revenue guidance of $10.4B to $11.2B versus about $10.5B expected, and weaker handset revenue; the posts differ on some figures.

items.name: Super Micro Computer
items.about: Builds AI and data-center servers and rack systems.
items.why: Super Micro fell about 5.7% to a close under $30, then slipped again after hours as it reported results. Posts say the numbers were strong but the stock fell in the same sell-off that hit AI hardware; the figures themselves were not confirmed.

items.name: ADMA Biologics
items.about: Makes plasma-derived immune globulin therapies for immune deficiency and infections.
items.why: ADMA fell about 6% in the session and bounced about 1% after hours. Posts refer to its earnings report around now and describe an unexpected drop; no specific results were confirmed.

items.name: Arm Holdings
items.about: Licenses the CPU designs used in most smartphones and a growing share of data-center chips.
items.why: Arm dropped 5.6% with chip stocks, then fell further after hours despite results. Posts quoting the release show revenue of $1.44B (+27%), license revenue up 50% and adjusted EPS of $0.52 versus $0.47 expected, with a December-quarter EPS outlook of $0.52 to $0.60 versus about $0.55 expected.

items.name: Coherent
items.about: Makes lasers and optical components, including transceivers used in AI data centers.
items.why: Coherent fell about 6% with other AI hardware names and was due to report after the close. Posts claim the results and guidance were strong, but those claims were not confirmed.

items.name: BioCryst Pharmaceuticals
items.about: Develops rare-disease drugs, including the hereditary angioedema medicine Orladeyo.
items.why: BioCryst slipped about 3.9% on higher chatter. The posts describe a rough day and thin volume but cite no news, so the reason is unconfirmed.

items.name: Kura Oncology
items.about: Clinical-stage cancer drug developer focused on menin inhibitors for leukemia.
items.why: Kura fell about 23% to $7.58. Posts say the drop followed conference (ASH) abstract data and point out cash of roughly $520M against a market cap near $690M, with earnings coming; the abstract details were not confirmed.

items.name: ImmunityBio
items.about: Cancer immunotherapy company whose Anktiva treatment is approved for bladder cancer.
items.why: ImmunityBio rose 7.8% to its high at the close. Posts say biotech ETFs rallied and expect earnings on Thursday, and also cite approvals of Anktiva in the EU, Saudi Arabia, Macau and the UAE.

items.name: Kratos Defense & Security
items.about: Builds drones, hypersonic test systems and defense electronics.
items.why: Kratos fell about 12% to near $36, a one-month low. Posts say earnings come Thursday after the close and that the stock is far below last year's highs; one post blames the election, which is unconfirmed.

items.name: CleanSpark
items.about: Bitcoin miner that is also building out power and data-center capacity.
items.why: CleanSpark fell about 17% along with other bitcoin-miner and AI-infrastructure names. Posts say its Texas build-out may be delayed, but no company announcement was found.

items.name: Direxion Daily Semiconductor Bull 3X Shares
items.about: Leveraged ETF that seeks three times the daily return of a semiconductor index.
items.why: SOXL lost about 9% on heavy volume as chip stocks fell, with Micron, Nvidia and Arm all lower. Being 3x leveraged, it moves roughly three times its index each day, so the move reflects a roughly 3% drop in semiconductors.

items.name: Berkshire Hathaway
items.about: Holding company with insurance, railroads, utilities and a large stock portfolio.
items.why: Berkshire climbed 4.1% to near $580 in a steady run. Posts speculate that money is rotating out of AI stocks and into value names or that cash is being deployed, but no company news was found.

items.name: Precigen
items.about: Gene and cell therapy company with an approved treatment for a rare airway disease.
items.why: Precigen slipped 3.8% ahead of its quarterly report, due around now per posts. Posts discuss revenue expectations of roughly $54M last quarter and the impact of a competing program; no results were confirmed.
